purpose: Next orthogonal public-information candidate wave centered on operational, regulatory, procurement, environmental and technology-disclosure clocks.

candidates.name: Federal procurement award-action shock × issuer exposure
candidates.hypothesis: Newly public federal contract or contract-modification actions may reveal demand/capacity changes for listed suppliers before broad market repricing.
candidates.construction: Use fixed USAspending transaction fields including award identifier, modification/action date, recipient and obligation amount; freeze a recipient-to-issuer map ex ante and use only transactions whose public availability boundary is proven, otherwise use a conservative next-session boundary. Distinguish base awards from later modifications.
candidates.next_gate: historical transaction/archive completeness, public-dissemination timing, recipient-to-issuer mapping, modification lineage
candidates.novelty_note: Demand-side operational shock; distinct from Treasury auction state and issuer filings.

candidates.name: FDA safety-labeling change shock × pharmaceutical issuer exposure
candidates.hypothesis: Newly public safety-related labeling changes may create issuer-specific regulatory information states distinct from clinical-trial-result and recall events.
candidates.construction: Use the FDA SrLC database's fixed event/section fields and application identifiers; freeze drug/application-to-issuer mapping before the historical window and preserve supplement/date/update fields without letting later database updates rewrite earlier states.
candidates.next_gate: historical archive completeness, exact public-posting/update semantics, NDA/BLA-to-issuer mapping, correction lineage
candidates.novelty_note: Post-approval safety-label state; distinct from Q179 clinical-trial publication and Q180/NHTSA recall.

candidates.name: CPSC consumer-product recall publication shock × issuer exposure
candidates.hypothesis: Newly public consumer-product recalls may transmit product-quality and liability information to listed manufacturers or brands before complete repricing.
candidates.construction: Use CPSC Recall API machine-readable recall records with fixed recall identifiers/date/product/manufacturer fields; freeze product-to-issuer identity and treat revisions/withdrawals separately from the original public state.
candidates.next_gate: historical API/archive completeness, exact recall public-availability clock, product/manufacturer identity mapping, revision/withdrawal handling
candidates.novelty_note: Non-automotive consumer-product channel; separate from Q180 NHTSA recalls and FDA drug recalls/labeling.

candidates.name: EPA enforcement/compliance state transition × facility issuer exposure
candidates.hypothesis: Newly refreshed public environmental compliance/enforcement states may reveal facility-level operating or liability changes before they are fully reflected in issuer disclosures.
candidates.construction: Use a fixed ECHO enforcement/compliance event taxonomy with the documented data-extraction/update boundary. Build a frozen facility-to-issuer graph; never substitute incident/inspection dates for public refresh availability and never let later refreshes backfill an earlier decision prefix.
candidates.next_gate: historical refresh/archive reconstruction, facility-to-issuer mapping, enforcement revision semantics, documented lag model
candidates.novelty_note: Environmental enforcement state; separate from OSHA workplace safety and physical-event channels.

candidates.name: Science-publication → patent-publication stage gap × technology issuer exposure
candidates.hypothesis: The relative public timing of science publication and patent disclosure may contain information about when innovation becomes externally observable, beyond a simple count of papers or patents.
candidates.construction: Match a frozen set of patent-paper pairs using deterministic bibliographic/title/identifier evidence; construct only a stage-order state comparing the first public science boundary with pre-grant/patent-publication/grant boundaries. Same-day or ambiguous chronology is excluded conservatively.
candidates.next_gate: candidate-specific patent-paper linkage census, science/publication timestamp semantics, patent-publication chronology, issuer mapping, revision handling
candidates.novelty_note: Stage-timing gap rather than Q186's citation-network topology or Q176's publication-burst level.

candidates.name: FDA drug-shortage publication state × manufacturer exposure
candidates.hypothesis: Newly public FDA drug-shortage states may reveal supply constraints, manufacturing interruptions or discontinuations for exposed listed manufacturers.
candidates.construction: Use fixed openFDA/FDA shortage records and product/manufacturer identifiers; preserve daily-list update semantics and distinguish shortage start/resolution dates from first public observation. Resolved/discontinued records must remain in their historical prefixes without current-page overwrite.
candidates.next_gate: historical archive completeness, first-public-observation timing, manufacturer/product mapping, resolution/discontinuation lineage
candidates.novelty_note: Supply-availability shock; distinct from Q188 regulatory labeling and Q179 clinical-trial state.
